slot.brief: Which compound has the highest/lowest lattice enthalpy from a set of ionic compounds (e.g. NaF vs NaCl vs KCl etc.) — ordering-style comparison MCQ.

stem: Which of the following ionic compounds has the highest lattice enthalpy?

verdicts.working: Lattice enthalpy magnitude increases with ionic charge product and decreases with ion separation. MgO and CaO have charge product 4; Mg²⁺ is smaller than Ca²⁺, so MgO has the highest lattice enthalpy.

working:
Lattice enthalpy increases with the product of ionic charges and decreases with interionic distance. MgO and CaO have +2/-2 ions, giving a higher charge product than NaF and NaCl, which have +1/-1 ions. Between MgO and CaO, Mg2+ is smaller than Ca2+ while both contain O2-, so MgO has a shorter interionic distance and higher lattice enthalpy. Therefore MgO has the highest lattice enthalpy.

Independent check: Lattice enthalpy magnitude increases with ionic charge product and decreases with ion separation. MgO and CaO have charge product 4; Mg²⁺ is smaller than Ca²⁺, so MgO has the highest lattice enthalpy.
solution: Lattice enthalpy increases with the product of ionic charges and decreases with interionic distance. MgO and CaO have the largest charge product, $|(+2)(-2)|=4$; since $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ is smaller than $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$, MgO has the shorter interionic distance and the highest lattice enthalpy.
